lede: The biggest thing on the government calendar this week is San Miguel County's Planning Commission taking up proposed changes to the Affordable Housing Impact Mitigation Fee — a fee structure that directly shapes whether workforce housing gets built here or not. Alongside that, TMVOA opens its three-meeting 2027 budget cycle and the county's intergovernmental meeting brings Telluride, Mountain Village, Ophir, and Norwood together for a regional large-projects check-in. On the lighter side, the week is packed: Art Walk, the Adult Spelling Bee, Wildbelly Fermentation Fest, and a FAFSA/financial aid workshop for families at the library.

notable.stake: First look at TMVOA's 2027 draft budget and completed 2025 audit.
Public hearings on a PUD land split and a 2026 budget amendment before Ouray BOCC.
County may reshape Affordable Housing Impact Mitigation Fee — affects all workforce housing projects.
Town will award the final Gondola Plaza West winter vending permit.
